transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Sofia — yeah, that ad was made for exactly that.  

So when a call hits your office and no one picks up, what usually happens next — does it go to voicemail, ring someone’s cell, or just... vanish?
User: Oh, hey! Voicemail, mostly. But who even checks those? It's like a black hole. Tell me more, I need this!
Agent: Gotcha, voicemail black hole — I hear that a lot.  

So roughly, how many calls a week would you say end up there instead of actually talking to you or your agents?
User: I don't really track it... maybe 25? Or 30? Wait, actually, yeah, let's go with 25.
Agent: Makes sense, 25 a week is a lot of people not actually reaching you.  

When one of those callers can’t get through and hits that voicemail black hole, do they usually try again later, or are they more likely to call another agent?
User: Honestly, they probably call another agent. It's so frustrating! I need a better way to handle this.
Agent: Yeah, that’s the killer — they’re not just missed calls, they’re new listings and buyers going to someone else.  

Mind if we put a real number to what that’s costing you each month — just a quick back-of-the-napkin math using your numbers?
User: Sure, sounds good! Let's crunch some numbers; I'm curious to see how much I'm losing each month.
Agent: Got it, love that you’re open to this.  

So with those 25 missed calls a week — if you actually picked up, what percentage of those do you think would turn into real opportunities for you, maybe buyers or listings — half, 60%, what feels right?
User: Probably around 60% could be real opportunities. It's crazy how much potential I'm missing out on!
Agent: Yeah, it adds up fast when you think about it that way.  

So for those opportunities — on average, what’s one deal worth to you when a caller actually turns into a client: are we talking more like $3k, $6k, $10k per side?
User: Oh, definitely around $6k per side. It's substantial, so I need to stop missing these calls!
Agent: Right, so with your numbers, that’s roughly $389,700 a month walking away from those missed calls — wild, I know.  

So… to actually plug that hole, I’d like to get you on a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how we turn those missed calls into booked appointments — is later today better for you, or tomorrow?
User: Oh, I'm busy next week—wait, actually, tomorrow works. Let's do tomorrow. What time slots do you have?
Agent: Awesome, we’ll lock in something for tomorrow.  

Quick thing first so I don’t mess anything up — what’s your last name, Sofia?
User: Oh, sure! It's Martinez. I almost forgot to mention, but let’s definitely confirm that time for tomorrow!
Agent: Got it, Sofia Martinez — thanks.  

Next thing so we can text you the confirmation: is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to reach you?
User: Oh, wait... yes, this number works. Just text me here. I'm in Mountain—oops, I mean Central Time.
Agent: Mhm, Central Time, perfect.  

Oh sorry, I didn’t get your number quite right — could you verify it real quick?
User: Oh, sure! It’s 555-123-4567. Let's make sure we've got the right time for tomorrow's call.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our side.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our side.
Agent: So, looks like our calendar’s being a bit stubborn with that number, but no worries — we’ll give you a call at this same number within the hour to lock in that 10:00 Central slot for tomorrow and make sure everything’s set. Really glad you called in, Sofia — anything else you wanted to ask before I let you go today?
